description:
P24 'feature ladder' probe (work/design/final_probes.json): compiles a CUMULATIVE ladder of 12 RPG IV/**FREE features, oldest/most-basic first, plus a 13th member (T0LAD12Q) that repeats rung 12 verbatim under CRTSQLRPGI instead of CRTBNDRPG, to find where PUB400's actual installed PTF level first stops accepting new syntax. Ladder order (per P24, matching final_probes.json exactly): **FREE -> DIM(*AUTO) -> FOR-EACH/%LIST/IN -> %SPLIT/%UPPER -> SND-MSG/ON-EXCP -> %CONCAT -> WHEN-IS -> DCL-ENUM -> CONST -> %HIVAL -> %DATE(*YYMD) -> ASSERT-T (also SQLRPGLE). Every rung N's source is rung N-1's source unchanged plus exactly one new block (see each src/t0ladNN.rpgle file's own header comment for its specific ilerpgref75.txt line citations), so a compile failure on rung N points at rung N's own new feature, not something inherited.

Why the wrapper does NOT stop at the first failure: verify/lib/clgen.mjs wraps each 'cl' step's command with its own MONMSG ... EXEC(DO) / GOTO <nextLabel> block (confirmed by reading clgen.mjs directly, lines ~97-109) - a step's failure jumps to the NEXT step's label, not to FAILSAFE, so every later rung is still attempted in the same connection even if an earlier rung's compile or run fails. Only an UNMONITORED message class would fall through to the wrapper's own top-level 'MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000) EXEC(GOTO CMDLBL(FAILSAFE))' and abort early - this is why every compile/run step below carries a deliberately wide MONMSG list (see 'MONMSG budget' below).

PTF/version findings verified directly against work/design/refs/ilerpgref75.txt (IBM i 7.5 ILE RPG Language Reference, 73451 lines) - these are the actual point of this probe, not guesses: SND-MSG and ON-EXCP (rung 5, literal message IDs only) are dated 'first half of the year 2022' (lines 2564-2566, 2595-2598), also available in 7.3/7.4 with PTF, so low risk. %CONCAT (rung 6) is dated 'second half of the year 2022' (lines 2164-2166). DCL-ENUM/END-ENUM (rung 8) is the ONLY place this task found a dated introduction of DCL-ENUM at all - lines 1501-1537, dated 'available with a compile-time PTF in the second half of the year 2025' - meaning rung 8 may already be a real failure point, not just rung 11. %DATE(*YYMD) (rung 11) is dated 'second half of the year 2025' (lines 1539-1555, 2463-2465) - matches the task's own hint that this may be newer/PTF-dependent. ASSERT-F/ASSERT-T (rung 12) is dated 'first half of the year 2026' (lines 1379-1408) - the SINGLE newest-dated feature in the whole ladder (newer than %DATE(*YYMD)), which is exactly why it is the last rung and also why it is worth checking separately under CRTSQLRPGI. A generic '*' message ID for ON-EXCP (NOT used by this ladder - rung 5 uses only literal IDs) is a SEPARATE, even-newer 'first half of 2026' enhancement (lines 1414-1436); this ladder deliberately avoids that form so it does not conflate two different PTF questions in one rung. DIM(*AUTO) (rung 2), FOR-EACH/%LIST/IN (rung 3, dated 'last half of year 2020', lines 2623-2648, so low risk), %SPLIT/%UPPER (rung 4), WHEN-IS (rung 7), CONST (rung 9) and %HIVAL (rung 10) are long-established RPG IV features with no comparable PTF-risk note found in the reference; they are included at these rungs only because that is where the design's own ladder order (P24) places them, not because this task expects them to be plausible failure points.

Syntax correction vs. the design doc's own shorthand: 'DIM(*AUTO)' (work/design/final_probes.json) is not literally what the reference shows - the documented syntax is 'DIM({*AUTO:|*CTDATA|*VAR:}numeric_constant)' (ilerpgref75.txt line 641) and every worked example includes a colon plus a maximum-element count, e.g. 'DCL-S array_auto CHAR(10) DIM(*AUTO:100);' (line 3277). Rung 2 therefore uses DIM(*AUTO:10), not a bare DIM(*AUTO).

Observability deviation from the task's literal 'QSYSPRT + EXCPT' instruction (matching verify/part05-gen-probe/src/t0eds.rpg): **FREE removes ALL fixed-form specs, including O-specs (ilerpgref75.txt lines 23280-23297: 'the entire source member must be free-form'), and EXCPT's exception-output mechanism is defined entirely on O-specs, so it has no free-form equivalent. This repo's OWN existing Part 6 **FREE lesson sources (src/qrpglesrc/f0605s.rpgle, f0609s.rpgle) already solved 'how do I confirm this ran, non-interactively' a different way for exactly this reason: send a message to the job log via the QMHSNDPM API (DSPLY is 5250-interactive-only). Every rung here reuses that exact, already-verified pattern (same QMHSNDPM prototype shape, copied from f0609s.rpgle, which itself cites ilerpgref75.txt lines 13744-13773) instead of QSYSPRT/EXCPT. This also has a concrete, harness-specific benefit: verify/lib/clgen.mjs runs each rung's CALL step inside the CL wrapper's OWN job, and that wrapper already dumps its own job log to the persistent VFYLOG table and SELECTs it automatically at the end of every connection (verify/README.md) - so every message a rung sends is captured for free, with no extra 'collect' step and no dependency on the still-unverified SYSTOOLS.SPOOLED_FILE_DATA path that spooled-file text would have required. Rung 5 (SND-MSG/ON-EXCP) also directly exercises the native SND-MSG opcode itself (not just the QMHSNDPM fallback), and wraps a MONITOR/ON-EXCP/CALLP block around a call to QMHSNDPM itself (already known-safe from rung 1 onward) rather than a made-up/nonexistent program name - the two reference files do not document which message ID a 'program not found' CALLP failure would raise, and guessing wrong there could produce an uncaught exception that aborts the whole connection early; see src/t0lad05.rpgle's own header comment for the full reasoning. Also note: the classic fixed-form CALL opcode is explicitly documented as 'not allowed - use the CALLP operation code' in free-form (ilerpgref75.txt lines 52461, 52518, 61551, 61667), which is why rung 5's 'build through the point where it would CALL' uses CALLP against a prototype, not CALL.

RPGLESRC record length: QRPGLESRC is NOT among the source files verify/tools/qclsrc/txsetup.clp auto-creates in the working library (only QDDSSRC is, per txsetup.clp lines 79-81), and this repo's only other QRPGLESRC reference (final_probes.json P04, DSPFD on <USER>1/QRPGLESRC) is a different, off-limits library (docs/probes.md: '<USER>1 ... 著者の私的な学習領域'), so this manifest cannot assume QRPGLESRC already exists with a known record length in <USER>2. The first file step below therefore uses batch.mjs's 'ensureSrcFile' mechanism to CRTSRCPF it first. CORRECTED (orchestrator, post-advisor-review): an earlier draft used RCDLEN 240 here, on the (unverified) claim that several lines exceed 112 bytes. Directly measuring every T0LADnn/T0LAD12Q source file's longest line found a maximum of 90 characters - well under 112. Since 'ensureSrcFile' only creates QRPGLESRC if it does not already exist, and every OTHER Part 6/7 manifest that also targets QRPGLESRC uses RCDLEN 112, a mismatched value here would silently truncate or corrupt whichever manifest runs SECOND (first-writer-wins) depending on execution order. Standardized to 112 to match every other manifest and avoid that fragility.

MONMSG budget: verify/lib/clgen.mjs emits each step's 'MONMSG MSGID(...) EXEC(DO)' line WITHOUT running it through the 80-column wrapping helper used elsewhere in the same file (confirmed by reading clgen.mjs directly) - the raw line must itself fit in 80 columns. With the fixed prefix/suffix clgen.mjs emits, at most 5 message IDs of 7 characters each fit (measured: 5 IDs = 79 chars, 6 IDs = 87 chars, which would silently corrupt the generated CL source). Every 'monmsg' list below uses at most 4 IDs, leaving headroom. Compile steps monitor CPF0000 (general command escapes)/RNF0000 (RPG compiler diagnostics - confirmed real prefix, ilerpgref75.txt lines 24603-24614, 34415-34437, 70766-70770)/RNS0000 or SQL0000 (compiler-command-level escape class; RNS0000 for CRTBNDRPG is an informed but UNVERIFIED guess - neither reference file documents the exact message ID CRTBNDRPG raises when a program object is not created because of compile errors, only that the behavior exists, ilerpgprogguide75.txt lines 34977, 35044)/MCH0000 (hardware/machine-check class, already used this way in verify/part05-gen-probe). CALL steps monitor CPF0000/MCH0000/RNQ0000 (ILE RPG inquiry-turned-escape messages, confirmed prefix at ilerpgref75.txt line 23259: 'inquiry messages issued by ILE RPG will start with the prefix RNQ, not RPG')/CEE0000 (Language Environment condition-manager escapes). None of this ladder's rungs are expected to actually raise any of these at runtime (every MONITOR/ON-EXCP block wraps a call expected to succeed) - the lists are a defensive net, not an expected path.

SQLRPGLE variant (T0LAD12Q): per the task instruction, ASSERT-T is ALSO compiled via CRTSQLRPGI. T0LAD12Q's RPG source is byte-for-byte identical to t0lad12.rpgle (a deliberate A/B comparison - see t0lad12q.sqlrpgle's own header comment for why it contains NO embedded SQL statement: this task grepped both ilerpgref75.txt and ilerpgprogguide75.txt for 'exec sql' and found zero hits, since embedded SQL syntax lives in IBM's separate SQL Programming manual, not either file provided to this task - rather than guess an unverified EXEC SQL statement and confound the ASSERT-T comparison, this member relies on CRTSQLRPGI's documented behavior of simply precompiling nothing and handing unchanged source to the RPG compiler when no embedded SQL is present). CRTSQLRPGI's own CL parameter names are ALSO not fully verified against these two references: ilerpgprogguide75.txt's only worked CRTSQLRPGI example (line 1307, 'CRTSQLRPGI MYLIB/MYPGM SRCSTMF(\'mypgm.sqlrpgle\') RPGPPOPT(*LVL1)') confirms the positional lib/name form and RPGPPOPT, but uses SRCSTMF (an IFS path), not SRCFILE/SRCMBR (a member) - this manifest's SRCFILE/SRCMBR/OBJTYPE/PGM keywords for a member-based compile are this task's own reasonable-but-unverified assumption (matching CRTBNDRPG's already-verified member-based usage elsewhere in this repo's manifests), flagged here rather than presented as confirmed. Full CRTSQLRPGI verification is separately tracked as this repo's own future P25 probe.

All 13 members are also actually CALLed (not just compiled), since every rung's MONITOR/ON-EXCP block only wraps calls expected to succeed - this gives a genuine 'did it run' signal via VFYLOG for every rung that compiles, not just 'did it compile'.

steps.label: CP12Q
steps.cmd: CRTSQLRPGI PGM(&LIB/T0LAD12Q) SRCFILE(&LIB/QRPGLESRC) SRCMBR(T0LAD12Q) OBJTYPE(*PGM) REPLACE(*YES)
